consensus_summary: No settled single meaning; coin is strictly context-dependent. The most developed common readings are the tribute denarius as stamped image/ownership/allegiance (humans as God’s image-bearers) and the lost coin as a precious lost sinner, alongside betrayal silver, widow’s mites as sacrificial giving, mammon, and occasional stewardship or provision senses.
book_summary: A person as the owner’s stamped image-bearer—refined like gold, bearing the sign/Name/image of God or the beast, assigned a value, and sought when lost; the recovered coin is a repentant sinner; human valuation differs from God’s.
consensus_core_identification: Context-dependent monetary token whose chief recognized senses are (a) image-bearing ownership marker or (b) lost person of value.
book_core_identification: Person as stamped image-bearer of the owner (God or beast), valued, refined, and sought when lost.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus keeps discrete pericope-bound senses separate and does not treat ‘coin’ as a unified anthropological symbol; book merges tribute-image and lost-coin motifs, then extends the same referent to census/valuation texts, metallurgical trial, and the eschatological God/beast marking.
material_contradiction: None; the book does not deny the contextual ownership or lost-sinner readings but reclassifies them as instances of one broader image-bearer category.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on the two dominant consensus strands (image-ownership and lost sinner). The book preserves those referents while materially widening extension and precision—adding refinement (1 Pet 1:7), dual ownership (Rev 13/14), assigned value (Ex 30/Lev 27), and valuation contrast—producing a refined rather than replaced or novel identification.
strongest_objection: Consensus insists on irreducible context-dependence and would regard the book’s single composite ‘person-as-coin’ as an over-unification that imports later texts by analogy rather than by direct biblical symbolism of ‘coin’.
